quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is correct?

options.text: You can complete a pass in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen only in safe, legal areas where passing is allowed. You must obey the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It means they see you.
It guarantees they will give you the right of way.
It does not guarantee they see you.
It is not worth trying to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact alone. A driver may look at you but still not notice your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item gives a rider the best face protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will not change.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should a passenger do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean when the rider leans.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold the rider.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the rider and lean with them. Sit as close to the rider as you can without crowding them. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: They do not need to leave space between bikes.
They should increase space between bikes.
They should reduce their normal space by half.
They should keep enough space around each bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should keep enough space around each bike.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When riding conditions are normal.
When the road is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Hold the grips loosely.
Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to get off the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Release the throttle and stay straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: When you are turning a motorcycle, what is true about stopping?

options.text: You have less grip available for braking.
You have more grip available for braking.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to brake while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less grip available for braking.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but only with great care. When your motorcycle leans to turn, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels that won't catch on foot pegs or road surfaces. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: When traveling on a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, the passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass another vehicle one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. All riders should follow this pattern until they have all passed safely.

questions.question: When you have mounted your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blindspots.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects your safety on the road. Good positioning helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is encouraged if traffic is heavy.
Is encouraged during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Is acceptable if the motorcyclist is comfortable with the move.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles and mopeds to pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
Can be distracting.
Don't help to improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: The primary source of information about your motorcycle should come from:

options.text: The motorcycle's former owner.
The owner's manual.
A library book about motorcycles.
A motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source of information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: When it is likely that other drivers may attempt to squeeze into your lane, you should:

options.text: Allow lane sharing.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane in heavy traffic discourages other drivers from squeezing into your space. Lane sharing is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of being involved in a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle. Always be ready to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what should they do?

options.text: One rider should finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
Multiple riders should pass the vehicle at the same time.
The last rider should wave to signal that no more motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider should finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass and rejoin the group before the next rider passes.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge at night than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it hard to see.
Use only one lane position.
Reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use your high beam headlight when there is no oncoming traffic. Be ready to change your lane position for safety.

questions.question: How do you get the shortest braking distance in a straight line?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit your view of the road.
They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
They are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Many people worry that helmets limit side vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets allow you to see everything you need for safe riding.
